title: Change Weaver
summary: Change Weaver implementation or contracts while preserving its narrative, requester, interactive-file-access, current-state, recovery, and deployment boundaries.

triggers: change the Weaver CLI or workflow
change Weaver state, recovery, or deployment
exclusions: add job search or application automation
publish a Weaver release without explicit intent

use_when: Weaver code, tests, CLI, repository contract, five-stage pipeline, validation, Nucleus requester boundary, private state, activation, maintenance, packaging, or documentation is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary narrative building or operation of the installed Weaver product.
The proposed feature is live job search, browser automation, application submission, publication, public-profile editing, or another workflow Weaver does not currently implement.
Release publication or installed deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: A minimal tested Weaver change whose product and operational documentation match the implementation and whose repository, Nucleus, recovery, privacy, and installation authorities remain explicit.
effects: Modifies Weaver source, tests, authored contracts, documentation, or packaging.
Requester-boundary changes may alter retained prompt content, permissions, correlations, compatibility, recovery, or deployment ordering and require corresponding Nucleus contract work.
Release and deployment remain separate actions that can commit, tag, push, replace installed selectors, or affect an active workflow.
authority: Weaver owns its current workflow, stage order, repository I/O, validation, cancellation intent, recovery, and installation behavior.
The narrative repository owns authored inputs and generated-output validity; Nucleus owns shared execution, authentication, and raw job history.
Weaver must not acquire publication, job-application, public-profile, or browser-workflow authority through an implementation shortcut.
success: The smallest owning Weaver component and every affected exact document agree.
Requester, state, activation, cancellation, validation, maintenance, packaging, rollback, and privacy proofs are updated in proportion to the changed boundary.
failure_and_recovery: Preserve a successfully written stage output even if a later stage or Nucleus runtime operation fails.
Do not add a direct-Codex fallback or a second repository-I/O process lineage to work around readiness or macOS file access.
Persistent or deployment changes require atomic replacement, tamper detection, rollback proof, and an explicit post-commit maintenance recovery path.
privacy: Tests, current state, Nucleus jobs, and diagnostics may contain complete narrative inputs, prompts, or generated outputs and must remain inside their private boundaries.
Release bundles contain only program, deployment, and Chancery documentation bytes, never narrative repository inputs.
steps: Read Weaver's `AGENTS.md` and the exact architecture, CLI, installation, and narrative-repository contracts for the affected behavior.

Before changing the Nucleus requester contract, persistent operational state, service lifecycle, deployment, or compatibility boundary, run `/Users/joey/.local/bin/nucleus manual` and identify the owning authority.
Implement the smallest change and update Weaver's operator-facing documentation in the same change whenever an operational fact changes.
Run `./ci.sh` and the exact deployment, recovery, or requester proofs affected by the change.
Treat release publication and installed deployment as separate actions requiring explicit authorization.
checkpoints: The change remains a narrative workflow feature rather than an unsupported job-application or public-service workflow.
The detached interactive-lineage worker remains the sole repository reader and writer, and Codex still receives only explicitly embedded inputs under its documented permissions.
Current-state and terminal-run semantics remain recoverable without automatic replacement model attempts.
CI passes, and release or deployment has not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Use the current version-matched Nucleus manual for shared requester and compatibility facts rather than assuming source or installed releases move in lockstep.
Scale tests and canaries to the actual change; repository validation, requester execution, worker activation, and installer rollback prove different authorities.
stop_when: A proposed change requires browser, computer-use, publication, or job-application behavior outside Weaver's current contract.
An incompatible requester or persistent-state change lacks migration, rollback, and recovery decisions.
The macOS repository-access boundary cannot be preserved with the interactive caller's process lineage.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying Weaver or cancelling an active installed workflow.
Adding live job search, application submission, publication, profile editing, or volatile UI automation.
